neu.name: Claude Code Changelog
zeilen: - Added `oidc.user_id_claim` to the Claude apps gateway, to identify people by an id_token claim other than `sub`, such as Microsoft Entra ID's `oid`
- Added click to send: in fullscreen, clicking the "to send now" hint under a queued message sends it right away, as its key does
- Fixed managed settings and organization policy not being fetched for the rest of the session after signing in from the VS Code extension
- Fixed Claude overwriting a very large CLAUDE.md, rules file or @-included file in a subdirectory after seeing only its start; Write now asks Claude to read it all or edit in place
- Fixed per-directory and `paths:` skills not being found after a Bash `cd` deeper into a git repository
- Fixed a rare case where the first reply after resuming a session in the terminal could be missing the next time the session was resumed
- Fixed a command with an invalid name stopping all commands from loading, which could leave `claude -p` with no output
- Fixed the Read tool sometimes failing on PDF pages with "pdftoppm failed: Could not write image" when the clean-up of old session files ran at the same time
- Fixed the spinner, OpenTelemetry `effort` values and transcripts naming a newly picked effort level during a task before the model applied it; they now show the level in force
- Fixed the `/model` and `/effort` cache warning saying the re-read waits for your next message; a change made while Claude is working can trigger it sooner
- Fixed some sessions showing as waiting on you when the last message only mentioned items waiting on you mid-sentence
- Fixed agent view restoring input text on the next launch after it was cleared with Ctrl+C just before exiting
- Fixed agent view reopening in shell mode after exiting with Ctrl+D from an empty `!` input
- Fixed vim mode `d`, `c` and `y` with a `gj` or `gk` count larger than the lines left deleting or copying text; like Vim, they now only move the cursor
- Fixed `/verify` showing a long description meant for Claude in `/help` and the `/` command menu instead of a short one
- Improved the prompt's effort indicator: a change made mid-task now says it may wait for your next message, and the note clears when it no longer applies
- Improved WebFetch errors in cloud sessions: a host that does not resolve is now explained as possibly outside the allowed network domains, so Claude names the host to allow

- Changed Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and Mantle to use the shorter system prompt for model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names and inference profile ARNs, even when they front Sonnet or Haiku; set `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT=0` to keep the full prompt

- Changed automatic model switches after a flagged message to also cover model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names; set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK=1` to turn them off
- Changed usage limit messages to call the 5-hour window the "5-hour limit" instead of the "session limit"
- Changed cloud sessions started from the CLI to get their names and branch names from the server

- Changed prompt and agent hooks to run at most 24 at a time per session, sub-agents included, plus at most 12 that have waited longer than their event's timeout; a `timeout` under 1 second now counts as 1 second
- Changed a subagent's `autoCompactWindow` to lower the window set by `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`, where it had no effect before; it still never raises that window
- Changed OpenTelemetry `mcp_server.name` to report the real name of fixed-URL remote MCP servers declared by plugins from the official Anthropic marketplace, instead of `custom`
- Changed Claude Code to stop sending the `claude_code.safety_event` OpenTelemetry event
- [VSCode] Fixed sessions ending on a bare exit code when your organization's settings couldn't be loaded or were refused at startup; the tab now says why and offers Retry or Sign in again
- [VSCode] Changed usage limit resets to show a clock time ("Resets at 3:10 PM") and to say "5-hour limit"
- [Cloud sessions] Added an effort level to the model picker when you create or edit a routine that runs in the cloud
- [Cloud sessions] Added a Bash editor with colors, line numbers and a Copy button to the setup script box in cloud environment settings
- [Cloud sessions] Improved the step shown when Claude adds a repository to a cloud session: opening it now shows a short table of what happened instead of raw JSON
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed resending an unchanged message after a failed send in a cloud session sometimes running it twice
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed a failed cloud environment creation showing its error only as a toast outside the open dialog; it now appears inside the dialog
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed Edit in a routine's menu on the Routines page going to the routine's page without opening its edit dialog
- [Remote Control] Fixed an unarchived Remote Control session showing as working until a computer reconnected; it now shows as idle
- [Claude Tag] Improved Claude Tag's retry notice in Slack to name the model in use, or say rate limits were hit, instead of a generic API error
- [Claude Tag] Fixed a Claude Tag channel's on/off switch and agent settings falling back to workspace defaults when an older private Slack channel goes public and gets a new ID
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack not replying in channels whose environment has network access set to None
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack sometimes posting a file in the wrong thread when it was answering in another thread of the same channel
- [Code Review] Fixed Code Review reviewing an outdated commit, or none at all, when GitHub delivered a push event late; it now reviews the pull request's current commit

neu.name: Claude Platform Release Notes
zeilen: * We’ve launched [Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-models-on-google-cloud/anthropic-managed), the Claude API operated by Anthropic and reached through your Google Cloud project. Google Cloud IAM controls access. Google Cloud Marketplace handles billing.

neu.name: Claude Platform Release Notes
zeilen: * We’ve released API version `2026-10-21`. [Migrating to API version 2026-10-21](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21) shows how to upgrade.

* We’ve released new versions of the [client SDKs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/overview) and the [`ant` CLI](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/cli/quickstart) that send API version `2026-10-21` by default: Python SDK 2.0.0, TypeScript SDK 1.0.0, C# SDK 13.0.0, Go SDK 2.0.0, Java SDK 3.0.0, PHP SDK 1.0.0, Ruby SDK 2.0.0, and `ant` CLI 2.0.0. See [Switch to 2026-10-21](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21#upgrade).

* The new SDK and CLI versions also have breaking changes that don’t depend on the API version, and they are licensed under Apache 2.0 instead of the MIT License. See [SDK and CLI changes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21#sdk-changes).

* We’ve added the `enforcement_status` and `enforcement_actions` fields to [user profiles](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-profiles), so you can see whether Anthropic has restricted or banned one of your end customers. To find the profiles that have an open restriction or ban, [list your profiles](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/user_profiles/list) with the new `enforcement_status[]` filter. See [Check whether Anthropic has restricted or banned a profile](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-profiles#check-whether-anthropic-has-restricted-or-banned-a-profile).

neu.name: Claude Platform Release Notes
zeilen: * We’ve launched [user profiles](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-profiles), so you can tell Anthropic which of your end customers each API request is for. If you operate a platform or gateway, or resell API access, a safety enforcement action can then apply to one end customer instead of your whole organization. The SDK and the `ant` CLI support the new [`/v1/user_profiles` endpoints](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/user_profiles).

* We’ve added [organization webhooks](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/organization-webhooks) to the [Admin API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/admin-api), in beta with the `webhooks-2026-10-07` beta header. Its [`/v1/organizations/webhooks` endpoints](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/webhooks) register webhook endpoints for two event types: one for when Anthropic restricts or bans one of your organization’s user profiles, and one for when the restriction or ban ends. To request access, contact your Anthropic account team.

* In Claude Managed Agents, the [`web_fetch` tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#available-tools) now follows your organization’s web fetch domain restrictions set on the [**Capabilities**](https://platform.claude.com/settings/capabilities) page of the Claude Console. A URL, including one reached by a redirect, must pass both the organization’s list and the `allowed_domains` or `blocked_domains` list on the agent’s `web_fetch` tool. See [Restrict web search and web fetch domains](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools-web-restrictions).

* In Claude Managed Agents, sessions follow your organization’s web search settings on the [**Capabilities**](https://platform.claude.com/settings/capabilities) page of the Claude Console: the **Allow web search** setting since October 6, and its web search domain restrictions since October 14. The agent receives only the search results that both the organization’s domain restrictions and the `allowed_domains` or `blocked_domains` list on the agent’s [`web_search` tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#available-tools) allow. See [Restrict web search and web fetch domains](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools-web-restrictions).

neu.name: Claude Platform Release Notes
zeilen: * We’ve added `capabilities.thinking.types.between_tools` to the [Models API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/models/list). `GET /v1/models` and `GET /v1/models/{model_id}` now report whether each model accepts `thinking: {type: "between_tools"}`, which turns off up-front thinking. See [Using the Models API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview#using-the-models-api).

neu.name: Claude Platform Release Notes
zeilen: * We’ve launched [OpenTelemetry export](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry) in beta, so you can trace Messages API requests and Claude Managed Agents sessions in your observability platform. The Claude SDK emits spans in Python, TypeScript, C#, Go, Java, PHP, and Ruby. To get spans from the API, [add an OpenTelemetry destination](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/opentelemetry/api#add-a-destination) in the Claude Console.

neu.name: Claude Platform Release Notes
zeilen: * You can now let a Claude Managed Agents agent use [dynamic workflows](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#dynamic-workflows), in beta with the `managed-agents-2026-04-01` beta header. For work with many pieces, such as reviewing hundreds of documents, the agent can write a workflow. A workflow is a program that runs many agents in phases and combines their results. The server runs it in the background as a workflow run. To [turn dynamic workflows on](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#turn-on-dynamic-workflows), set the agent’s `multiagent` field to `{"type": "multiagent_20261001", "workflows": {"type": "enabled"}}`. To guide the agent, tell it in its system prompt when to start a run. Follow each run through `workflow_run.*` events on the session’s event stream. See [Workflow runs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/workflow-runs).

neu.name: Claude Platform Release Notes
zeilen: * We’ve lowered the price of prompt cache reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from $0.20 USD to $0.10 USD per million tokens: 0.05x the base input price instead of 0.1x. Cache writes and all other prices are unchanged. See [Prompt caching pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#prompt-caching).

* We’ve launched **Claude Haiku 5.5** (`claude-haiku-5-5`), our most capable model tuned for high-volume and latency-sensitive work. It has a [1M token context window](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows), 128k max output tokens, and [adaptive thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking) with the [effort parameter](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort). It’s available on the Claude API, [Claude in Amazon Bedrock](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-amazon-bedrock), [Claude Platform on AWS](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws), [Claude on Google Cloud](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-models-on-google-cloud/google-managed), and [Claude in Microsoft Foundry](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry). See [What’s new in Claude Haiku 5.5](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/haiku-5-5/whats-new-haiku-5-5).

* With `limited` networking, creating a session fails with a 400 error when an enabled web tool’s `allowed_domains` has an entry not within `allowed_hosts`. So does a session update that adds such an entry. An `allowed_hosts` entry matches one exact host unless it starts with `*.`, so `docs.example.com` is not within `["example.com"]`. To fix the error, add the host to `allowed_hosts` or remove the entry from `allowed_domains`. See [Restrict web search and web fetch domains](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools-web-restrictions).

* In Claude Managed Agents, the [`web_fetch` tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools#available-tools) now fetches only URLs that have already appeared in the session, for example in the text of a user message, in a `web_search` result, or in a page that `web_fetch` returned earlier. This reduces the risk of data exfiltration. A URL that appears only in Claude’s own output, the agent’s system prompt, an attached document, or the output of a tool such as `bash`, `read`, or an MCP tool does not count: a `web_fetch` call for it returns a `url_not_in_prior_context` error result to the agent. To let the agent fetch a URL, send it in the text of a `user.message` event.

neu.name: Claude Platform Release Notes
zeilen: * We’ve added `capabilities.server_tools` to the [Models API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/models/list). `GET /v1/models` and `GET /v1/models/{model_id}` now report whether each model accepts the web search and code execution tools. To check whether a model accepts the code execution tool, read `capabilities.server_tools.code_execution`. The top-level `capabilities.code_execution` reports whether code can call your request’s other tools. See [Using the Models API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview#using-the-models-api).
